description: Cross-binding conformance for §6.6.5 inline-test assertions on an array OBSERVED that NO LIVE EQUATION CONSUMES. An inline test's natural target is a quantity computed FOR the test — a tendency, a flux, a diagnostic — which by construction nothing else reads. The asserted `diag` is such a dead observed, and `chain` is a dead observed that reads another dead one. The Julia build published neither: the elementwise array-observed fold inlines such an observed into its readers and drops its equation, and a dead one has no readers to be inlined into, so `BuildInspection.observed_exprs` never carried it and every assertion failed with `array state '<name>' has no cells in var_map` — on a document whose defining equations Rust and Python both evaluate. Julia is the reference binding; its `run_pde_tests` minted golden/dead_observed.json, and the Rust (`esm test`) and Python (`run_pde_tests`) runners reproduce the same five actuals.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator / inline PDE-test runner
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator / inline PDE-test runner

fixtures.note: The only state is `u`, integrated with a zero right-hand side, so the trajectory is constant and every assertion is exact at any time under any pinned solver family — a divergence here is a semantics divergence, never an integrator one.
